package_info.why_malicious: The subdomain cdn2.cocoapods.org, previously used by CocoaPods, was abandoned but its DNS records still pointed to GitHub Pages. Attackers hijacked the subdomain to host a casino website, which could have been used for phishing, malware distribution, or other malicious activities under the guise of a trusted brand.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious casino website content hosted at https://cdn2.cocoapods.org/
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user or automated system navigates to cdn2.cocoapods.org, the DNS resolves to a GitHub Pages site controlled by the attacker, serving a casino website. This could be used to phish users, distribute malware, or impersonate CocoaPods.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: A well-known infrastructure subdomain for a software supply chain tool is serving unrelated gambling content, indicating a hijack.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate CocoaPods subdomains should only serve official package or CDN content, not third-party or gambling sites.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be serving documentation, package files, or static assets for CocoaPods.
key_indicators: Abandoned subdomain still pointing to third-party hosting (GitHub Pages)
Content unrelated to the original service (casino/gambling site)
Potential for phishing, malware, or brand impersonation

attack_chain.action: Attacker discovers abandoned subdomain cdn2.cocoapods.org still points to GitHub Pages.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker claims the subdomain on GitHub Pages.

attack_chain.action: Attacker sets up a GitHub Pages repository and configures it to serve content at cdn2.cocoapods.org.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious or unwanted content is now served from a trusted subdomain.

attack_chain.action: Malicious casino website is hosted and accessible at cdn2.cocoapods.org.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential phishing, malware distribution, or user deception.

behavioral_signatures: Abandoned subdomains of trusted brands serving unrelated or suspicious content
DNS records for subdomains pointing to third-party hosting platforms (e.g., GitHub Pages) with no official content
Sudden change in content type (e.g., from package hosting to gambling/phishing)
file_indicators: Presence of CNAME or A records for subdomains pointing to GitHub Pages or similar services
Unexpected HTML/JavaScript content on infrastructure subdomains
network_indicators: Network requests to cdn2.cocoapods.org (or similar abandoned subdomains) serving non-official content
Unusual traffic to known developer infrastructure domains with unexpected content types
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor DNS records for critical infrastructure subdomains to ensure they do not point to third-party hosting unless actively used. Regularly scan subdomains for unexpected content changes, especially for developer or package manager domains. Alert on sudden changes in content type or hosting provider for trusted subdomains. Use web crawlers to verify that subdomains serve only expected content and not unrelated or suspicious material.
